questions.stem: What causes a Data Skew Issue?
options: Data not being distributed evenly across the nodes in a cluster
Indexes being disabled on large tables
Poorly written join conditions in a query
Low data quality in the source systems
A lack of data standardisation across datasets
questions.explanation: A Data Skew Issue arises when data is not distributed evenly; uneven distribution at cluster level degrades query performance even when the query, joins and indexes are all correct.

questions.stem: What is the Data Skew Issue normally referred to as in the Data Science domain?
options: Data Coupling
Uneven Load Balancing
Data Enrichment
Skewed Data Distribution
Massive Parallel Processing
questions.explanation: In the Data Science domain the same idea is known as Skewed Data Distribution, a concept related to Statistics.

questions.stem: Which kind of query is said to suffer the most from a Data Skew Issue?
options: Simple single-table lookups
Queries with joins
Queries that only count rows
Queries run against a single node
Queries on freshly loaded datasets
questions.explanation: Data skew heavily degrades query performance, especially for queries that involve joins.

questions.stem: Why does uneven data distribution slow queries in a Massive Parallel Processing (MPP) cluster?
options: Because the cluster has to rebuild every index before the query runs
Because skewed data forces the query to run on a single node only
Because uneven data automatically triggers a full backup
Because MPP switches to a non-parallel mode when data is unequal
Because MPP cannot be utilised properly, so the compute power of all nodes is not fully used
questions.explanation: When data is not spread evenly across all nodes, MPP cannot be utilised properly and not all of the nodes' compute power is used, slowing the query response.

questions.stem: Which activity is named as one of the main reasons for a Data Skew Issue?
options: Adding more CPU and RAM to the cluster
Enabling indexes on frequently joined columns
Data Enrichment, such as inserts, updates and delete tags that move data between locations
Running queries during peak business hours
Applying data standardisation rules
questions.explanation: Data Enrichment moves data from one location to another, creating an imbalance of data across the nodes in a cluster.

questions.stem: In the ten-node cluster example for data skew, three nodes end up with 2% of the data each while three others gain an extra 8% each. What happens when a query runs?
options: All ten nodes work until the 2% nodes finish, after which the remaining data is effectively processed by only seven nodes
The query fails because the nodes no longer hold equal shares
The three nodes with 2% each take the longest to complete
The cluster automatically redistributes the data before running the query
The query runs entirely on the three heaviest nodes
questions.explanation: The query uses all ten nodes until the lightly loaded nodes are done; the data on the heavier nodes then takes longer because MPP is effectively running on seven nodes, so the full compute power is not utilised.

questions.stem: What exercise is normally run to address the Data Skew Issue after a data pipeline execution or Data Enrichment?
options: Index rebuilding
Data standardisation
Adding more nodes to the cluster
Load Balancing, so data is evenly redistributed across the cluster
Purging the oldest data
questions.explanation: Load Balancing exercises are run so that after each pipeline execution or enrichment the data is evenly redistributed across the cluster.

questions.stem: What is described as the first thumb rule for query performance in the era of Cloud and MPP?
options: Queries should always be limited to a single node to avoid contention
When a query runs, all possible compute power should be utilised
Data should be kept on as few nodes as possible
Every query should be cached before it is executed
Compute should be added before storage
questions.explanation: The first thumb rule is that all possible compute power should be utilised when a query runs, which is only possible when data is evenly distributed across the nodes.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT listed as a type of Skewed Data?
options: Skewed Right (Positive)
Skewed Left (Negative)
Skewed Outlier
Skewed Narrow Range
Skewed Diagonal
questions.explanation: The listed types include Skewed Right, Skewed Left, Symmetric, Evenly Distributed, Two Mode Symmetric, Two Mode Non-Symmetric, Narrow Range, Wide Range and Outlier; Skewed Diagonal is not among them.

questions.stem: A query runs exceptionally well until 99% and then hangs for hours, and adding CPU, RAM and nodes does not help. Which explanation matches this symptom?
options: The joins in the query are incorrect
The data quality of the dataset is poor
A Data Skew Issue: the data is unevenly distributed across the cluster
The indexes on the tables have been disabled
The dataset is too small to benefit from parallel processing
questions.explanation: This is the classic symptom of a Data Skew Issue, where a correct query with correct joins and indexes still performs badly because the data is unevenly distributed across nodes.
